Irene / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. Procurement asked for a short "playbook" that explains how your per-token volume discounts work in practice (we need a clean example we can show finance).

Attached is our 12-month conservative forecast (Q4–Q3) — totals are in tab "summary". Our ask: can you show 2 worked examples against our numbers: one using a marginal (breakpoint) ladder and one using a blended effective rate, plus a short note on true-up mechanics and credits? We'd prefer to see how the effective $/1k tokens shifts as we move through breakpoints.

Also, any recommended breakpoint sizing when you see a profile like ours (large initial burst in Q1 then steady-state)? We're trying to decide whether to push for aggressive breakpoints or a simpler blended anchor that finance can sign off on.

Can you get something back by EOD Thursday? Procurement will use it for our internal pricing committee.

Hi Tom — thanks for the forecast, this is great context. Quick plan:

- I'll assemble a short playbook with two worked examples (marginal ladder vs blended effective) using your forecast figures.
- Karthik will add the recommended breakpoint sizing and the true-up/credits language.
- Ben will confirm operational items (invoice cadence, trial credits).

High level guidance up front: for bursty profiles we often recommend a short ramp of breakpoints (e.g., smaller first breakpoint to cover the burst, larger subsequent buckets for steady-state) and a marginal pricing ladder because it preserves the supply-side incentive and is easier to show incremental savings. Blended is simpler for finance but can obscure marginal economics — we'll show both.

I attached a one-page draft (pricing-playbook-draft-v1.pdf) with a template we can adapt — will update with numbers and send by Thursday EOD. If you're open, propose a 30-min sync on Thursday 10:00am PT to run through it together before the committee.

Irene / team — looping in a compact worked math section we can drop into the playbook. Using numbers that map to the forecast totals (rounded): expected tokens = 18,500,000,000 (18.5B) over 12 months with Q1 burst ~6B. Proposed ladder (example only):

- Breakpoint A: 0–5B tokens @ $0.00040 / token
- Breakpoint B: 5B–12B tokens @ $0.00032 / token
- Breakpoint C: >12B tokens @ $0.00026 / token

Marginal calculation (what the bill shows):
- First 5B @ $0.00040 = $2,000,000
- Next 7B @ $0.00032 = $2,240,000
- Remaining 6.5B @ $0.00026 = $1,690,000
- Total = $5,930,000 -> Effective $/token = $5,930,000 / 18.5B = $0.000320 (or $0.32 / 1k tokens)

Blended calculation (single blended rate to cover whole volume):
- If we offered a blended rate of $0.00034 / token to make billing clean:
- Total = 18.5B * $0.00034 = $6,290,000 -> Effective = $0.00034 / token (higher than marginal result above)

Why marginal often wins for us: it shows immediate savings as you cross breakpoints and aligns incentives: early burst sits at higher rate, steady-state benefits at lower marginal. Blended is predictable and simpler for procurement and accounting (one line).

True-up mechanics (short):
- Quarterly true-up based on actual tokens vs committed corridor.
- If usage < committed floor, standard approach is either (a) credit accrual applied to next invoice up to X months or (b) invoice for shortfall at agreed floor rate.
- If usage > committed cap, overage charged at published on-demand rate or at next-breakpoint marginal, depending on contract.

Modeling note: for Acme's bursty profile I recommend a smaller first breakpoint (5B) to avoid a large portion landing at the highest slab, then wider middle slab to capture steady-state. We'll surface sensitivity: if Q1 is 30% higher/lower, here's delta on effective rate.

I'll add the worked math into the playbook and attach an example workbook.

—Karthik

Quick ops notes to include in the playbook:

- Invoice cadence: monthly with quarterly true-up (we'll include sample invoice lines).
- Trial credits: offer a 90-day $75k pilot credit to cover initial Q1 burst — this makes it easier for procurement to greenlight. Pilot credit applied as invoice offset; any unused credit expires after 90 days.
- Corridor clause: propose +/-15% corridor on forecast for the first 2 quarters to allow smoothing without automatic shortfall billing.

I'll also add a short checklist for procurement (PO terms, SOC2 evidence, IP/data clauses, KMS integration note).
